title: The Guggenheim fellowship
summary: Gil says getting the Guggenheim was great and that the award was nine thousand dollars.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: I think that there must be some joys that came though when it was clear to you that other people were recognizing what you were trying to do as something of superior quality.

I think the Guggenheim (Koggenheim?) because the Guggenheim (Koggenheim?) is an extremely difficult award to get. And it doesn't make one rich by any means, but it does come as, at least in the scholarly world, it comes as a recognition of....
I loved getting it. It was
Yes, I would think that would be one of the.....
I got nine thousand dollars. I'd asked for more but nine was okay. I was glad to get it. It's about the best one thing you can get I think.
Yes I think it is. And certainly in terms of the honor that comes along with it, it's quite a distinguished award.

I haven't had occasion to lean on that yet but I'll be glad to when I can. They gave me a letter you know saying that I was a Guggenheim (Kouganheim?) Fellow and a "to whom it may concern" type of letter. I keep it with me though just in case I may need it.
